name: Quadruped · Spot
summary: Boston Dynamics Spot in MuJoCo: learns to stand, walk and climb (PPO, GPU or CPU), then patrols a warehouse, hearing and seeing incidents and raising alarms
help:
Boston Dynamics Spot (MuJoCo Menagerie, BSD-3: 12 joints, joint limits; masses scaled to Spot's real 32.5 kg, hip and knee torques from Boston Dynamics' joint data) in MuJoCo, the physics engine robotics research uses. It learns by trial and error (PPO), many robots at once on an NVIDIA GPU (MuJoCo Warp) or on the CPU, then patrols a warehouse.

What to do:
- Learn to stand: it starts lying where a fall left it (on its side, on its back) and learns to roll over, get up and stay up.
- Learn to look around: its feet planted, it aims its front cameras with its legs: body up, down, left, right, lower.
- Learn to walk: a trot at the speed and turn asked. On the Obstacle course (slopes, stairs up and down, curbs, rough ground, moving tiles, ice) it also gets an elevation map of the ground ahead from its cameras and learns to use it.
- Walk: the newest policy drives it live in the 3D view: speed, way round, push it, reset.
- Patrol the warehouse: a session of surveillance (30 minutes by default) in a 42 x 25 m warehouse: four loading docks, three aisles of pallet racking, staging, an east floor, a mezzanine office reached by 7 steps and a 15 % ramp, a conveyor crossed by a step-over bridge, a dispatch platform with steps and a 12.5 % ramp, aisles cluttered with pallets and cartons to step over. It walks a round through the areas asked for (A* on a map of the floor, followed with its walking policy), stops at checkpoints to look (with the look-around policy: up to the top racks, down to the floor), hears (sound falling with distance and through racking) and sees (110° cameras, 14 m, line of sight). A sound or a movement sends it to look: a carton fallen, a door in the wind, a forklift with a badged driver are logged; a person without a badge raises the alarm (siren, operator alerted) and it follows them, keeping its distance, until they leave. At the end it goes back to its dock. It writes incident_report.md, incidents.json and patrol_log.csv.

Areas: all, or names (Loading docks, Aisle A, Aisle B, Aisle C, Staging area, East floor, Dispatch platform, Mezzanine office), or your own: Name: x y; x y (metres; x 0 at dock 1, along the south wall; y 0 at the dock aisle, toward the north wall).

The patrol is always in the physics: every step is the walking policy's, in MuJoCo, and you can push the robot (Push, then click on it). It uses the policies wired to Policies, or else those the training runs left on the machine; with a policy that learned the flat floor only, its round keeps to the flat floor. Good walking needs GPU training: about 1 to 2 hours per stage on one NVIDIA GPU (4096 robots); a few minutes on the CPU only shows it learning.

Controls in the 3D view: Patrol: Acknowledge alarm, Intruder drill, End patrol, Push, Push strength, Speed. Walk: Speed, Push, Reset.

inputs.label: Policies
inputs.help: Spot's policies (.pt): walking, stand-up, look-around. Learn: carries on from the newest. Walk, Patrol: the newest of each

outputs.label: Policy
outputs.help: spot_walk_[course_]…, spot_standup_… or spot_look_<date>_<NN>.pt: the best policy (network, scaling, optimizer, score)

outputs.label: Learning curve
outputs.help: training.csv (Learn to walk), standup.csv (Learn to stand) or look.csv (Learn to look around)

outputs.label: Patrol report
outputs.help: Patrol: incident_report.md, incidents.json, patrol_log.csv (once a second: where, what it was doing, battery)

params.label: What to do
params.help: Learn to stand: get up. Learn to look around: aim its cameras with its legs. Learn to walk: trot. Walk: live. Patrol the warehouse: the surveillance session

params.label: Robot
params.help: Spot: 1.1 m long, 32.5 kg, 12 joints (MuJoCo Menagerie; masses and torque limits set to Boston Dynamics' figures)

params.label: Run on
params.help: auto: an NVIDIA GPU machine (MuJoCo Warp; PyTorch with CUDA installed on its own if missing). CPU: any machine, fewer robots

params.label: Ground
params.help: Learn to walk, Walk. Obstacle course: slopes, stairs up and down, curbs, rough ground, moving tiles, ice

params.label: Robots learning at once
params.help: Learn: at most 512 on the CPU

params.label: Minutes
params.help: How long it learns, walks or patrols (Patrol: 30 is a night round)

params.label: Pushes up to (m/s)
params.help: Learn to walk: a shove every 5 to 10 s; 0: none

params.label: Replay every (s)
params.help: Learn: how often an episode is replayed in the 3D view

params.label: Seed
params.help: Patrol: which night (where and when incidents happen); 0: a new one each run

params.label: Training
params.help: Continue: from the newest policy wired in (or a stopped run's checkpoint on this machine). Start over: from nothing

params.label: Walking speed (m/s)
params.help: Walk, Patrol: the speed it walks at (the view's slider changes it)

params.label: Heading (degrees)
params.help: Walk: on the obstacle course beyond ±90° it goes round clockwise; on the flat floor, the way it walks

params.label: Walking policy
params.help: Walk, Patrol: which walking policy wired in to use (empty: the newest)

params.label: After a fall
params.help: Walk, Patrol: with a stand-up policy wired in it gets up on its own; else it is set on its feet 3 s later

params.label: Areas to patrol
params.help: Patrol: all, or names (Aisle A, Loading docks…), or your own as Name: x y; x y (see the help)

params.label: Incidents
params.help: Patrol: how often something happens (cartons, doors, forklifts, intruders)

params.label: Patrol starts at
params.help: Patrol: the clock time shown and reported (hh:mm)

params.label: Pace
params.help: Patrol: As fast as it can writes the report in seconds (nothing to watch live)
